ai.description: Whitaker's Boa reaches 60 cm. It is reddish-brown with dark, irregular dorsal blotches and a pale underside. Key features include a blunt, wedge-shaped head and a short, thick, prehensile tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Eryx whitakeri* is best distinguished from the common *Eryx johnii* by its distinct, dark-brown to blackish blotched pattern, whereas *E. johnii* is typically uniform brown.
ai.habitat: Whitaker's Boa inhabits the moist deciduous forests and coastal regions of the Western Ghats, typically found at low to moderate elevations under leaf litter or loose soil.
ai.behavior: Whitaker’s boa is a nocturnal, burrowing specialist that spends much of its time buried in loose sand, emerging primarily at night to ambush small lizards and rodents.
ai.reproductionNotes: Whitaker's Boa is ovoviviparous, typically giving birth to a litter of 6–8 young. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with parturition in the following months.
ai.distributionRemarks: Whitaker's Boa is endemic to the Western Ghats of peninsular India, primarily occurring in the states of Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu at elevations up to 1,000 meters.
